target_customer: Governments and public services, funded by foundations and grants rather than customers
problem: Public interest organizations lacked data science capacity; Bayes Impact first ran fellowship teams of data scientists on social problems and later built open source products for public services.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by grants and donations
product_category: Data science for social good nonprofit; open source public service software

founders.name: Paul Duan
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2014-07-15) says he had volunteered at homeless shelters and worked on ad click prediction at internet companies.

founders.name: Andrew Jiang
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he had worked with the City of New York on civic technology.

founders.name: Eric Liu
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he worked at a venture capital firm focused on data science.

technical_complexity.rationale: Data science projects for public bodies, later open source AI agent platforms; complexity is moderate and fit to public sector constraints.

defensibility.rationale: As a nonprofit with open source code the edge is relationships with public institutions and mission trust, not a technical moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No takeover; as a nonprofit it was not a target. DataKind and similar data for good groups ran in parallel.

market_need_then: TechCrunch framed it as supplying data scientists to social justice groups with problems but no data capacity; YC accepted it as a nonprofit in its Summer 2014 batch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven; says it aims to change the world through algorithms

branding.community_and_virality: Hackathons and fellowship coverage in VentureBeat and Dataconomy in 2014 and 2015; Ashoka fellowship for the founder.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in data for good and French public service circles, with press and foundation backing, but no brand origin or community evidence.

pivots.from: Fellowship style data science consultancy for nonprofits
pivots.to: Product driven NGO building digital services for governments
pivots.why: A 2015 profile described the shift; reasons not detailed in the opened sources. Date is the profile year.

outcome_analysis: Bayes Impact launched in 2014 as the nonprofit in YC Summer 2014 with $100K from YC and Teespring, moved from fellowship projects toward products for governments, and in 2026 builds an open source AI platform for public services with Google.org and Gates Foundation support. Income reportedly fell in 2019 but it remains active, so it is a survivor of an unusual nonprofit model.
notes: Competitors list left empty: the TechCrunch launch article names none, and DataKind and Chicago DSSG appear only in a 2015 MIT analysis, later than the batch. The Google.org item is from a January 2026 Les Echos headline listed on the company site; amount and currency not stated, and the page does not make clear if every item is a grant. InfluenceWatch reports revenue above $960K in 2017 and roughly $100K in 2019, not verified against filings. CB Insights lists $50K total, which is incomplete. The pivot date is approximate. Wikipedia and search results list Pascal Corpet as a third founder alongside Duan and Liu; TechCrunch names Andrew Jiang instead, so the conflict is noted and only TechCrunch names are listed.
